newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bakrie says may sell PT Arutmin stake.
newsitem.headline: Bakrie says may sell PT Arutmin stake.

text.p: Indonesian conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers said on Thursday it was considering selling its 20-percent stake in coal mining firm PT Arutmin.
"We are considering getting out of PT Arutmin," Bakrie president-director Tanri Abeng told reporters. "Bakrie has already been approached by four potential buyers."
He declined to give further details.
PT Arutmin is 80-percent owned by The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd. Bakrie bought its 20-percent stake in PT Arutmin for $40 million in 1995.
Tanri declined to give details on the firm's net profit forecast in 1997.
Bakrie has not published its full year 1996 financial results.
It posted a net profit of 120.02 billion rupiah in 1995 against 102.81 billion rupiah in 1994.

Tanri said the firm had signed a Letter of Intent to sell its 49-percent stake in Indocopper on Thursday to PT Nusamba Mineral Industri, but it would conclude the sale only after gaining approval from an Extraordinary Shareholders meeting expected on March 12.

Nusamba Mineral is part of the Nusamba Group, which is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto. Timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, who heads Nusamba, and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto each have a 10-percent stake.
